QuestionText: If yesterday was Tuesday, what day of the week will it be tomorrow?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: If yesterday was Tuesday, then today is Wednesday. Therefore, tomorrow will be Thursday.

QuestionText: A clock shows exactly 4:00 PM. What type of angle is formed between the hour hand and the minute hand?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Each hour gap on a clock face represents 30 degrees. At 4:00, there are 4 hour gaps between the hands (4 × 30° = 120°). An angle greater than 90° but less than 180° is an obtuse angle.

QuestionText: If the 3rd day of a month is a Sunday, what day of the week will the 17th day of the same month be?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Days of the week repeat every 7 days. If the 3rd is Sunday, adding 7 days means the 10th is a Sunday, and adding another 7 days means the 17th is also a Sunday.

QuestionText: Anil's school exam started at 10:15 AM and lasted for exactly 2 hours and 30 minutes. At what time did his exam end?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Adding 2 hours to 10:15 AM brings you to 12:15 PM. Adding the remaining 30 minutes to 12:15 PM results in 12:45 PM.

QuestionText: How many days are there in total in a leap year?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: A standard calendar year has 365 days, but a leap year adds one extra day to February, totaling 366 days.

QuestionText: If 5 days ago was Thursday, what day is it today?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Counting 5 days forward from Thursday: Friday (1), Saturday (2), Sunday (3), Monday (4), Tuesday (5). Wait, let's recalculate: Thursday + 5 days = Tuesday.

QuestionText: How many minutes does the minute hand of a clock take to travel all the way around from the number 12 back to the number 12?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: One complete rotation of the minute hand around the entire clock face represents 1 full hour, which is exactly 60 minutes.

QuestionText: If a non-leap year starts on a Monday, on what day of the week will that same year end?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: An ordinary year has 365 days, which equals 52 weeks and 1 extra day. Because of this 1 extra day, an ordinary year always ends on the exact same day of the week that it began.

QuestionText: A movie starts at 8:45 PM. If the movie runs for 115 minutes, at what time does it finish?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: 115 minutes can be rewritten as 1 hour and 55 minutes. Adding 1 hour to 8:45 PM brings you to 9:45 PM. Adding another 55 minutes brings you to 10:40 PM.

QuestionText: How many months in a single standard calendar year have exactly 31 days?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: There are 7 months with 31 days: January, March, May, July, August, October, and December.

QuestionText: If today is Friday, what day of the week was it 15 days ago?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: 15 days can be broken down as 2 full weeks (14 days) plus 1 extra day. Going back 14 days lands on a Friday. Going back 1 more day lands on Thursday.

QuestionText: At what exact time between 1:00 and 2:00 do the hour hand and minute hand of a clock point in perfectly opposite directions to form a straight line?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: To be perfectly opposite, the hands need a 30-minute separation distance. At 1 o'clock, the hour hand is at 1, so the opposite side is around the 7 mark (35 minutes). Because the hour hand moves slightly as the minutes tick, the exact straight line happens at roughly 1:38.

QuestionText: Rohan's birthday is on the last day of September. What is the date of his birthday?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: September is a month that has exactly 30 days. Therefore, the final day of the month is September 30th.

QuestionText: If the hour hand of a clock moves from 2 to 6, how many degrees has it turned in total?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The hour hand turns 30 degrees for each hour that passes. Moving from 2 to 6 is a jump of 4 hours. 4 × 30 degrees = 120 degrees.

QuestionText: How many times does a digital clock show the digit sequence '11:11' over a complete 24-hour day cycle?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The sequence appears twice a day: once in the morning (11:11 AM) and once at night (11:11 PM).

QuestionText: If June 4th is a Tuesday, what date will the next Tuesday be?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: To find the next matching day of the week, add exactly 7 days to the current date: 4 + 7 = June 11th.

QuestionText: A clock loses 5 minutes every single hour. If it is set correctly at 12:00 noon, what time will the faulty clock display when the actual real-world time is 4:00 PM?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Between 12:00 PM and 4:00 PM, 4 hours pass. Since the clock loses 5 minutes each hour, it will lose a total of 4 × 5 = 20 minutes. 4:00 PM minus 20 minutes leaves the clock reading 3:40 PM.

QuestionText: How many days are left in the month of October after October 24th?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: October has 31 days in total. The number of remaining days after the 24th is calculated as 31 - 24 = 7 days.

QuestionText: If the minute hand of a clock points directly at the number 9, how many minutes past the hour does it indicate?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Each number on a clock dial represents a step of 5 minutes. When pointing at 9, it indicates 9 × 5 = 45 minutes past the hour.

QuestionText: If February 28th is a Sunday in a non-leap year, what day of the week will March 2nd be?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: In a non-leap year, February has exactly 28 days. Therefore, the next day (March 1st) is a Monday, and March 2nd is a Tuesday.

QuestionText: How many times do the hands of a clock pass directly over each other (overlap) between 12:00 noon and 3:00 PM?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The hands overlap exactly at 12:00 (noon). They overlap again slightly after 1:05 PM, and a third time slightly after 2:10 PM. This means they overlap 3 times within that window.

QuestionText: If a train is supposed to arrive at 7:10 AM but is running 45 minutes late, what time will it arrive?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Adding 45 minutes to 7:10 AM: 50 minutes brings you to 8:00 AM, so 45 minutes brings you up to 7:55 AM.

QuestionText: What date is exactly one week before Independence Day in India (August 15th)?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: One week equals exactly 7 days. Subtracting 7 days from August 15th yields 15 - 7 = August 8th.

QuestionText: A clock is showing 6:30. What angle do the hour and minute hands make with each other?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: At 6:30, the minute hand is pointing exactly at 6. However, the hour hand has moved halfway between 6 and 7. Since a full hour gap is 30 degrees, half of that gap is exactly 15 degrees.

QuestionText: How many total hours are there in a single complete 3-day weekend?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Each day contains 24 hours. For a duration of 3 days, the calculation is 3 × 24 = 72 hours.

QuestionText: If the second day of a 30-day month is a Friday, how many Sundays will there be in total during that month?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: If the 2nd is a Friday, the 3rd is Saturday and the 4th is Sunday. The Sundays fall on the 4th, 11th, 18th, and 25th of the month. Adding 7 more days would equal 32, which goes past the month's 30-day limit, leaving a total of 4 Sundays.

QuestionText: If a modern electronic clock displays the time as 14:20 in 24-hour format, what time would a standard 12-hour AM/PM clock show?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: To convert 24-hour times greater than 12 into 12-hour PM times, subtract 12 from the hours: 14 - 12 = 2, making the time 2:20 PM.

QuestionText: How many seconds pass in a time window of exactly 5 minutes?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Each minute contains 60 seconds. For a length of 5 minutes, the calculation is 5 × 60 = 300 seconds.

QuestionText: If today is Tuesday, what day of the week will it be exactly 70 days from now?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: 70 is a perfect multiple of 7 (10 × 7 = 70), meaning it marks a stretch of exactly 10 full weeks. Because it lands perfectly on a weekly loop, the day remains Tuesday.

QuestionText: A clock chimes once at 1:00, twice at 2:00, three times at 3:00, and so on. How many total chimes will it make between 12:30 PM and 4:30 PM on the same day?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The hour marks that fall inside this time window are 1:00, 2:00, 3:00, and 4:00. The clock will chime 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 times.

QuestionText: If New Year's Day (January 1st) falls on a Wednesday, what day of the week will January 31st be in that same month?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The difference in days is 31 - 1 = 30 days. Dividing 30 by 7 gives a remainder of 2 days (4 weeks × 7 = 28 days). Counting 2 days forward from Wednesday lands on Friday. Wait, let's recalculate: 1st is Wed. 1+28=29th is Wed. 30th is Thu. 31st is Fri. The correct option is D.

QuestionText: How many times does the minute hand pass the number 6 on a wall clock during a full 12-hour cycle?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The minute hand completes 1 full circle every single hour. In a 12-hour period, it completes 12 full rotations, passing the number 6 exactly 12 times.

QuestionText: If a leap year begins on a Monday, what day of the week will the next calendar year begin on?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: A leap year has 366 days, which breaks down into 52 weeks and 2 extra days. Because of these 2 extra days, the day of the week shifts forward by two slots, meaning the next year starts on a Wednesday.

QuestionText: What is the total number of minutes in half a day?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: A full day contains 24 hours, so half a day is 12 hours. Since each hour has 60 minutes, the calculation is 12 × 60 = 720 minutes.

QuestionText: If a person sleeps at 9:30 PM and wakes up at 6:00 AM the next morning, how long did they sleep?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: From 9:30 PM to 12:00 midnight is 2 hours and 30 minutes. From midnight to 6:00 AM is 6 hours. Combining these durations gives 2 hours 30 minutes + 6 hours = 8 hours and 30 minutes.

QuestionText: Which of the following years is guaranteed to be a leap year?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Leap years occur every 4 years and are evenly divisible by 4. 2024 is divisible by 4 (2024 ÷ 4 = 506), making it a leap year.

QuestionText: If the calendar date is May 15th, what will the date be exactly 3 weeks later?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: 3 weeks equals exactly 21 days (3 × 7 = 21). Adding 21 days to May 15th: 15 + 21 = 36. Since May has 31 days, subtract 31 from 36 to find the date in the next month: 36 - 31 = June 5th.

QuestionText: How many rounds does the hour hand of a clock complete in one full day?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: The hour hand takes 12 hours to complete 1 circle around the clock dial. In a 24-hour day, it completes 24 ÷ 12 = 2 full rounds.

QuestionText: If the 1st of January is a Friday, what day of the week will the 8th of January be?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Adding exactly 7 days to any date lands on the same day of the week: 1 + 7 = 8th, so it is also a Friday.

QuestionText: A stopwatch ran for 180 seconds. How many minutes is this equal to?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Since there are 60 seconds in 1 minute, divide the total seconds by 60: 180 ÷ 60 = 3 minutes.

QuestionText: If tomorrow is Saturday, what day of the week was it 2 days before yesterday?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: If tomorrow is Saturday, today is Friday, and yesterday was Thursday. Two days before Thursday was Tuesday.

QuestionText: What name is given to a duration of 10 years?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: By definition, a span of 10 consecutive years is called a decade.

QuestionText: A classroom wall clock currently displays 11:50. How many minutes are left before it strikes 12:00 noon?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: An hour has 60 minutes. 60 - 50 minutes leaves exactly 10 minutes remaining until the next full hour mark.

QuestionText: If a company workshop runs from the morning of April 28th to the evening of May 2nd, for how many total calendar days does the event run?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: April has 30 days. The workshop runs on April 28, 29, and 30 (3 days), plus May 1 and 2 (2 days). 3 + 2 = 5 days total.

QuestionText: If the calendar year is 2026, when will the next leap year arrive?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Leap years occur in multiples of 4. The closest year after 2026 that divides evenly by 4 is 2028.

QuestionText: How many days are there in the month of July?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: July is one of the standard calendar months that contains 31 days.

QuestionText: If a clock's hands show a time of quarter past 6, what numerical values are they closest to?
Options: A) Hour hand at 6, Minute hand at 3
B) Hour hand at 6, Minute hand at 15
C) Hour hand at 3, Minute hand at 6
D) Hour hand at 9, Minute hand at 6
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: 'Quarter past 6' means 15 minutes past 6 o'clock (6:15). At 15 minutes, the minute hand points directly at the 3 mark, while the hour hand is near 6.

QuestionText: How many full weeks are there in a standard calendar year of 365 days?
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: Dividing 365 days by the 7 days in a week equals 52 weeks with 1 day left over.

QuestionText: If an analog wall clock falls to the ground and stops ticking at twenty minutes to 8, what numerical positions were the hands locked at?
Options: A) Hour hand near 8, Minute hand at 8
B) Hour hand near 7, Minute hand at 4
C) Hour hand near 8, Minute hand at 4
D) Hour hand near 7, Minute hand at 8
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: 'Twenty minutes to 8' means 7:40. At 40 minutes, the minute hand points directly at the number 8, and the hour hand has crawled close to 8.

QuestionText: If a certain month has exactly 29 days, what year cycle type must it be?
Options: A) An ordinary year February month
B) A leap year February month
C) A leap year January month
D) A standard non-leap year March month
SubTopic: Days & Dates, Days of the Week, and Clock Logic
Explanation: February is the only calendar month that can change its length. It holds 28 days in regular years and 29 days during a leap year.
